title: decoupled-window-sampler-continuous-batcher-guard
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Context: Continuous-batcher deployments occasionally experience head-of-line starvation when a small number of KV-heavy requests (long KV-pin phases) intersperse with many short requests. Existing fairness mechanisms bias by queue age or slot reservations which either starve long jobs or degrade tail latency for short requests. Motivation: We need a low-risk, incremental change that (1) prevents starvation for age/priority-insensitive KV-heavy flows, (2) avoids global reordering that harms throughput, and (3) is easy to roll back. Design summary: Introduce a 'decoupled window sampler' that separates admission sampling from dequeue ordering. Admission sampling operates on fixed-duration windows per queue-shard and selects a small, jittered fraction of long-running/kv-heavy candidates to be admitted into a protected reservoir. Dequeue ordering continues to run the existing continuous-batcher dequeue (to preserve throughput-friendly coalescing) but consults a lightweight reservoir tag: if a request is in the protected reservoir and has waited beyond a soft-threshold, it gains prioritized dequeue eligibility without preempting in-flight coalesces. Key ideas: - Decouple admission: sampling uses per-shard lightweight histograms (slot-age, kv-pin-duration, seq-len-estimate) to probabilistically mark requests for reservoir admission rather than changing queue order on enqueue. - Windowed jitter: windows are 50-200ms (configurable) with jitter to avoid sync across shards. - Reservoir size caps: reservoir caps per-shard to a small fraction of active slots (default 4%) to keep throughput stable. - Soft-threshold + prioritized dequeue: an admitted request exceeds a soft wait threshold (configurable per-service SLO) => it is eligible for prioritized dequeue that preempts the next idle slot but does not interrupt an ongoing coalesce. - Fallbacks: if prioritized dequeue fails (no free slot within timeout), request falls back to normal queue path; admission marker expires to avoid indefinite priority. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'decoupled_window_sampler_v1' and a per-cluster sampling rate. Staged rollout: canary 1% of traffic on dedicated clusters, 10% after metrics look good, full rollout after 7 days with automated rollback on regressions. Tests & safety: strict unit tests for sampler determinism, integration tests for reservoir expiry and prioritized dequeue, chaos test that flips sampling rate under load, and cost-aware benchmarks to ensure throughput is not regressed. See related Linear tasks ENG-4621 (continuous-batcher starve analysis) and ENG-4690 (production rollout plan). Checklist: [x] design doc updated with algorithm details; [x] unit/integration tests; [x] perf benchmark harness runs; [x] runtime flag + telemetry; [x] rollout playbook in ops runbook. release_notes: Add decoupled window sampling to continuous-batcher: reduces starvation of KV-heavy requests while preserving coalescing throughput. Feature is gated and off by default.
benchmark_summary: Benchmarks (kv-mix, 50/50 short:short=8-12ms / kv-heavy=120-250ms): 95th tail for short requests reduced from 210ms -> 72ms in mixed load; long-request median wait reduced 46%; end-to-end throughput unchanged within 1.5%. Cost delta < 0.4% at default reservoir cap.
review_thread: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Can you clarify why admission is probabilistic rather than deterministic? Author response: Probabilistic admission avoids global reordering and keeps per-shard memory bounded; determinism would require heavier coordination and risks throughput regression.

Ravi Patel (reviewer): How does this interact with current slot reservations for premium customers? Author response: Reservoir caps are applied per-tenant when slot reservations exist; for reserved slots we lower sampling rate to avoid stepping on reserved throughput. Added integration test for reservation interaction.

Elena Novak (reviewer): Concern about telemetry cardinality from histograms. Author response: we sample histograms at a low rate and aggregate to coarse buckets; added a config knob to disable histogram metrics in pressure scenarios.
Miguel Torres (approved): LGTMs after small nits addressed. Ravi Patel (approved): Verified bench harness results.
testing: Unit tests (sampler determinism, expiry), integration (reservoir lifecycle + prioritized dequeue), chaos tests (flip sampling rates + induce KV pin storms), e2e benchmarks in bench lab. CI: full test matrix passed on linux-amd64 and linux-aarch64. Canary run (1% traffic) for 48h with no SLO regressions before 10% rollout.
